reading.rtitle: Email from Grace (Kigali) -- Can You Help This Week?
paras: Hi Carlos, I hope you are well. Next week a European buyer is visiting our office in Kigali, and we need some help from the Brazil team. I have six requests for you. Please tell me what you can do and what you can't do this week.

First, can you send me the EUDR maps of the twelve farms in Minas Gerais? Second, can you translate the farm checklist from Portuguese into English? Third, can you provide the training records of the producers? Fourth, can you join a video call with the buyer on Thursday?

Fifth, can you sign the new supplier form? Sixth, can you present the Brazil results in the call? I know you are very busy with the project, so it is OK to say no. I can wait until Friday for the documents. Thank you, Grace.
reading.source: Grace, Sustainability Manager, Sucafina Rwanda -- internal email, A1 reading

listenings.text: My English is getting better every week. Today I can read a sustainability report in English, and I can write a short email to a colleague. I can present the numbers of our farms in a meeting, slowly and clearly. But I can't speak fluently yet, and I can't understand fast speakers on a call. When I can't understand, I say: Can you repeat that, please? My goal for this year is simple. In December, I want to explain the EUDR to a buyer without help.

Hi Carlos, this is Grace from Kigali. Thank you for your email. Good news: the buyer can visit on Thursday, not on Wednesday. So you can join the call on Thursday at ten in the morning, Brazil time. I can present the Rwanda results, and you can present the Brazil results. About the supplier form: no problem, your manager can sign it next week. Thank you, and see you on Thursday.

extra_audio.text: First, I read the six requests from Grace. Then, I say yes: I can send the EUDR maps today. Next, I explain: I can translate the checklist, but I need two days. After that, I say no politely: I can't sign the supplier form. Finally, I ask a question: can I join the call on Thursday?
